title: G Launcher theme
$comment: PHASE D7. Written AFTER the shape shipped, so it documents what exists rather than what was planned. Its job is not documentation: it is catching the add-a-field-in-seven-of-eight-places failure that has already cost two evenings. See docs/theme_authoring.md for the checklists.
$comment_strict: additionalProperties is FALSE throughout, and that is a deliberate difference from the runtime parser. The app is tolerant on purpose: an unknown key from a newer CDN theme must be ignored, never fatal, because a downgrade must not black-screen someone's home screen. This schema runs in CI against OUR OWN themes, where the same tolerance would silently swallow a typo. `splsh` is not forward compatibility, it is a broken splash nobody notices for a month.

id.$comment: Stored in prefs as the per-theme key and used in the icon cache id. NEVER rename a shipped id: it orphans every override and every desklet placement a user has made under it. Version the id instead (ubuntu-24-04.v2) when the icon block changes.

shell.$comment: A DESKTOP ENVIRONMENT, not a distro. Most new distros are a palette plus a wallpaper plus a boot log on top of one of these, which is why adding Kali or Mint costs no Dart.

tier.$comment: Presentation only. Real entitlement is resolved natively against the signed index (CdnIndex.isUnlocked); a theme cannot unlock itself by claiming free.

minAppVersion.$comment: The theme registry falls BACK to Ubuntu rather than throwing when this is not met, so an old client meeting a new pack degrades instead of breaking.

chromeFamily.$comment: Omit to inherit ChromeFamily.defaultForShell. Only set it when a distro's chrome genuinely differs from its shell family.

paletteLight.$comment: The LIGHT variant, optional. `palette` remains the dark one and keeps its name: renaming it to paletteDark would have been tidier and would also have broken every bundled theme.json and every pack already published. A theme without this block simply has no light mode; EffectiveTheme falls back to `palette` rather than inventing a pale version of it.

wallpapersLight.$comment: Wallpapers for LIGHT mode. Empty or absent means use `wallpapers` in both. The launcher runs TRANSPARENT over the system wallpaper, so a light palette over a dark photograph does not read as a light theme: it reads as the chrome having lost its colour.

fonts.$comment: Font families this pack ships, registered at runtime. A CDN theme cannot edit pubspec.yaml, so naming a family in `typography` is not enough for anything that did not ship in the APK. A family with no name or no files is dropped at parse.

files.$comment: BARE FILENAMES for an installed pack: PackPaths.installedFile refuses a separator, so every asset inside a pack is flat.

gestures.$comment: Gesture id to action id. String values only; anything else is dropped rather than fatal. The action ids are NOT enumerated here because bindingFor screens them beside the enum, which is the same arrangement terminal aliases have except that those ARE enumerated, because a bad terminal alias fails silently and a bad gesture does not.

wallpapers.$comment: The FIRST entry is applied once, on first use of the theme, and never again (LauncherPrefs.wallpaperInitialized). Order matters for that reason alone.

wallpaperMeta.$comment: How each wallpaper meets the screen, KEYED BY THE SAME STRING that appears in `wallpapers` or `wallpapersLight`. A sidecar map rather than richer `wallpapers` entries because that array is a published wire format and the string is an identity elsewhere: prefs.wallpaperCurrent stores it, the rotation worker stores a list of them, wallpaperContentStamp digests them. Every key is OPTIONAL and so is the whole block; a wallpaper with no entry is centred with the app default fit, which is exactly what every pack did before this existed. A key naming a wallpaper this theme does not ship is never looked up rather than an error, matching the runtime parser.

wallpaper.$comment: LEGACY single-wallpaper form. Still parsed so a theme already on someone's phone keeps working. Do not author new themes with it.

wallpaperMeta.$comment: Framing for ONE wallpaper. The user owns framing and overrides all of this the moment they drag, so this is a STARTING POINT, not a lock: it exists because the author knows where the subject is and the app does not. An empty object is legal and means the same as omitting the key.

fit.$comment: OMIT to take the app default rather than writing 'cover'. Null and 'cover' are not the same fact: null means this pack expressed no opinion and should follow the default if it ever changes, 'cover' means this pack chose it. Unknown values degrade natively to 'cover' at runtime, but this schema runs against our own themes in CI where a typo should fail rather than degrade.

focalX.$comment: A FRACTION OF THE SOURCE IMAGE, not pixels and not screen coordinates. Pixels break the moment decodeSampled picks a different sample size, which it does on every different screen. 0.5 is the centre and is the default.

focalY.$comment: As focalX, down the image. This is the one that usually matters: distro art tends to be horizontally centred already and vertically off, which is why a tall logo render lands behind the dock.

zoom.$comment: 1 is the whole frame; above 1 keeps less of the picture. NEVER BELOW 1, which would ask for a region larger than the image and produce either a degenerate crop rect or bars the fit did not ask for.

color.$comment: #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB. Alpha FIRST, matching Android, not last as CSS does it. Getting that backwards produces a theme that looks fine until something translucent renders.

assetPath.$comment: Repo-relative. A path not under assets/ will not be bundled, and Flutter asset directories are NOT recursive: adding assets/themes/foo/ to a theme means adding it to pubspec.yaml too. That exact omission shipped a terminal theme that silently fell back to Ubuntu.

bgBottom.$comment: Load-bearing beyond the wallpaper gradient: it is the boot-log canvas, the splash background and the drop-shadow colour every bare desklet uses. A wrong value here shows up as a boot screen that does not look like this distro.

display.$comment: Must match a family declared in pubspec.yaml EXACTLY. Bundled today: Ubuntu, UbuntuMono. An unknown family does not throw; Flutter silently substitutes, which is why a typo here is invisible until someone looks closely.

logo.$comment: TWO variants, named for the SURFACE they sit on, not for their own colour. `light` is drawn as authored on a light surface; `dark` is tinted to palette.onDark. Getting the naming backwards is the usual mistake.

grid.$comment: The DESKTOP grid, which under the authentic decision holds desklets and never app icons. Defaults to 5x4 when omitted, which is why the terminal theme can leave it out entirely.

iconScale.$comment: CLAMPED to this range by IconSizing.parseScale at runtime. Enforced here so an author is told rather than silently corrected.

icons.$comment: Passed straight to native. The launcher never renders icons in Dart. ADDING A FIELD HERE TOUCHES EIGHT PLACES and missing two of them fails SILENTLY (works once, then serves stale bitmaps forever) - the checklist is in docs/theme_authoring.md.

backgroundColor.$comment: null is MEANINGFUL and not the same as absent-by-accident: it means keep the app's own adaptive background layer.

backgroundGradientEnd.$comment: Requires backgroundColor, which is the near end. Set without it, the renderer keeps the app's own background and ignores this.

brandTreatment.$comment: A STRING, NOT AN ENUM, in the wire format, because Pigeon numbers enums before classes and a third enum would renumber every class in launcher_api.dart. Kept a string here too so the schema does not promise something the codec cannot deliver. Known values: brandPlate, themePlate; unknown degrades to brandPlate.

durationMs.$comment: CLAMPED to 400-1500 by SplashSpec's constructor. A CDN theme cannot decide your desktop takes eight seconds to appear.

terminal.$comment: This distro's terminal. ADDITIVE and optional: palette holds six colours and none of them is an ANSI colour, so a terminal cannot be drawn from it. Absent falls back to TerminalSpec.defaultForShell. Having a terminal is INDEPENDENT of shell being tui, because the Terminal app is a drawer entry and gnome/plasma/tiling/aqua distros all have drawers.

appLabel.$comment: The drawer entry's label. SHORT, because the drawer renders it in list, grid, cube and horizontal layouts and the narrowest gives it one line under an icon. Beyond 24 it ellipsises.

prompt.$comment: Tokens: {user} {host} {cwd} {distro} {exit}. An unknown token renders LITERALLY rather than being stripped, so an authoring mistake is visible instead of silently eating a segment.

scrollbackLines.$comment: CLAMPED to 500-50000 by TerminalSpec's constructor. Enforced here so an author is told rather than silently corrected. A CDN theme cannot decide your phone holds fifty thousand lines in memory.

aliases.$comment: Names bound to actions this build already has. A pack can NEVER express shell, a URL, a package name or an intent here: a downloadable theme that could ship executable commands would be remote code execution on a home screen. Duplicates are dropped on parse, first declaration wins.

terminalPalette.$comment: Role colours (ok, warn, err, dim) are NOT authored. They are read out of ansi at indices 2, 3, 1 and 8, because in every real terminal green IS success and red IS failure: that is what the program emitting the escape code means. Four authored duplicates would be four chances to disagree with the sixteen sitting beside them.

ansi.$comment: Standard order: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, then the eight bright variants. INDEX IS THE SGR CODE OFFSET, so the order is not a style choice. A short or malformed array fails the whole terminal block rather than being padded: padding puts some escape codes on a colour nobody chose, which reads as a rendering bug instead of an authoring one.

name.$comment: Lowercased on parse. Must not collide with a command name or alias in the registry; the runtime resolves the builtin first, so a colliding alias silently does nothing.

action.$comment: The wire names of CommandAction. ENUMERATED HERE and asserted against the enum by terminal_spec_test, the same arrangement kindId has: the runtime keeps an unknown id and simply fails to bind it, so without this list a typo would vanish silently. ADDING AN ACTION MEANS UPDATING THIS LIST AND THAT TEST.

args.$comment: Scalars only. Anything else is dropped on parse. A nested structure here would be a small language, and a small language in a downloadable pack is how this stops being data.

kind.$comment: An unknown kind degrades to `plain` at runtime rather than failing to parse. Enumerated here so a typo in OUR themes is caught rather than silently flattened.

offers.$comment: Which kinds this distro exposes in the picker, in picker order. An empty or absent list falls back to the shipping set, so a theme predating this block does not get an empty picker.

starter.$comment: The desktop laid out the FIRST time this theme is chosen, and never again. No ids: they are minted on apply, so two installs of the same pack cannot share one.

config.$comment: Free-form, per kind. Validated and clamped on READ, so an unknown key is ignored rather than fatal.

skins.$comment: Per-kind override, MERGED over DeskletSkin.defaultFor(shell, kind). Partial is the point: a theme that wants a bigger clock writes timeSize and inherits everything else.

skin.$comment: surface/font/accent are structural and constrained. Everything else is a free-form prop read with a fallback (num_/flag/text), so additionalProperties stays open here on purpose - this is the one place in the schema where a new key must not need a schema edit.

kindId.$comment: ENUMERATED ON PURPOSE, even though the runtime keeps unknown kinds rather than deleting them. A typo (`clcok`) would otherwise vanish from the picker silently, which is exactly the failure class this file exists to catch. ADDING A KIND MEANS UPDATING THIS LIST - see the checklist in docs/theme_authoring.md.
